one_line: Morph lets an agent reshape a site's native interface around a user's goal.
what_it_does: Composes task-specific shopping, travel, and news interfaces from trusted site data and native components.
leverage_rationale: The claimed product is specifically a shared, persistent interface-composition model in which structured WebMCP capabilities change what the site becomes; ordinary UI automation would not reproduce this as reliably or natively.
leverage_evidence: Description says the assistant selects supported components/actions and composes an interface that remains part of the original site.
Three distinct domains are described with structured transformations of existing result sets.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent multi-domain concept and quantified example outcomes, with live demo and frame sheets, but the supplied text has no transcript and visual inspection was unavailable during review.
execution_evidence: Live demo is reported alive.
Description gives concrete Wayline, Hearth & Home, and The Current workflows and result counts.
impact_rationale: It addresses a broad and credible web problem: fixed interfaces hide answers that users need, while preserving site trust and interactivity.
impact_evidence: Explicit shopping, travel, and news use cases.
Examples convert conventional result grids/feeds into goal-specific views.
creativity_rationale: The central interaction model—having the site become the interface needed for the task—is a memorable and ambitious synthesis beyond adding chat to a webpage.
creativity_evidence: Natural-language goal to native, editable, inspectable interface composition is the core concept.
Concept is pursued across three deliberately different website types.
usability_note: Potentially intuitive goal-based interaction, though persistence/editability details are claimed rather than observed.
red_flags: Visual/video evidence could not be independently assessed; no transcript supplied.
standouts: Strong cross-domain demonstration of a genuinely different web interaction model.
Native data and component governance is unusually well aligned with WebMCP.
advance_reason: High-leverage, highly creative concept with credible practical value and a coherent claimed implementation.

one_line: SkillSpace is a human-curated local library of reusable agent skills.
what_it_does: Lets people browse and inspect skill provenance, curate a local Skillspace, and lets agents search and retrieve relevant skills through typed WebMCP tools.
leverage_rationale: Typed browser tools and shared local state directly replace prompt copy/paste and brittle integrations for skill discovery and retrieval.
leverage_evidence: Four focused tools are specified: search_skills, get_skill_metadata, get_skill, and list_my_skills.
IndexedDB local-first Skillspace is shared between human curation and agent retrieval.
execution_rationale: The architecture is coherent and implementation details are specific, but there are no submitted frame sheets or gallery images, limiting end-to-end execution confidence.
execution_evidence: Live app and public source repository are provided.
Claims Zod validation, sanitized outputs, feature detection, and shared domain services.
impact_rationale: Agent users and teams have a real need for discoverable, trusted, versioned instructions; the human-curation boundary is a credible fit.
impact_evidence: Provenance, source, version, license, and content inspection are explicit user functions.
Retrieving only relevant skills addresses context overload and trust concerns.
creativity_rationale: A browser-native, human-controlled skill library with live agent retrieval is a fresh synthesis, though the registry/library category is established.
creativity_evidence: Human curation and agent discovery share a local capability context.
Untrusted skill content is explicitly not executed.
usability_note: Clear browse/inspect/curate model; actual polish and retrieval flow are not evidenced visually.
red_flags: No video frame sheets or gallery images submitted, so central workflow is not visually evidenced.
standouts: Local-first shared state makes the WebMCP rationale concrete.
advance_reason: Strong agent-infrastructure relevance and meaningful WebMCP delta despite thin execution evidence.

one_line: Rundown lets agents create and edit live dashboards through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Provides dashboard widgets, filters, data sources, sharing, and a tool surface for agent-authored visual dashboards.
leverage_rationale: Agents can inspect datasource fields and perform structured dashboard edits while the visual artifact updates in real time; this is materially more reliable than clicking a complex editor.
leverage_evidence: Every dashboard-editor action is claimed to be a WebMCP tool.
Example chains describeDatasource followed by addWidget with realtime visible effects.
execution_rationale: The scope is coherent and the packet includes video frame sheets plus a live demo, but no transcript and no observed visual details limit certainty about end-to-end completeness.
execution_evidence: Live demo reported alive and three video sheets supplied.
Claimed support for data sources, widgets, filters, controls, and sharing.
impact_rationale: Dashboard creators and client-facing marketing teams have a concrete recurring need to turn intent into useful visual reporting with less manual setup.
impact_evidence: Description identifies product engineers, agencies, and clients as users.
Use case targets campaign dashboards and recurring data flows.
creativity_rationale: Agent-authored visual dashboards are a fresh interaction layer over a known dashboard-builder category, with a sensible realtime visual/text bridge.
creativity_evidence: The dashboard remains the visual artifact carrying the creator's intent.
Datasource inspection before widget creation is a thoughtful agent workflow.
usability_note: Natural-language dashboard creation could reduce editor friction; collaborative and data-connection details are unverified.
red_flags: Execution claims are not backed by a transcript and visual frames could not be independently assessed.
standouts: Good mapping between typed agent actions and visual dashboard state.
advance_reason: Credible, high-value dashboard workflow with a substantial WebMCP delta.

one_line: PassCraft lets an agent reserve event tickets and generate a QR pass.
what_it_does: Exposes ticket selection, validation, total calculation, reservation, and dynamic event-pass generation to a browser agent.
leverage_rationale: Typed booking and validation tools can make a multi-step reservation flow more reliable, but the same outcome is generally possible through ordinary UI automation.
leverage_evidence: A named reserver_pass_evenement tool is described.
Claimed flow includes ticket type validation, total calculation, and pass generation.
execution_rationale: The single-page scope and claimed QR output are coherent, but no video frames were submitted and the packet offers only packaging plus description evidence.
execution_evidence: Live demo reported alive.
Implementation is described as a lightweight autonomous SPA with Tailwind and Lucide.
impact_rationale: Event attendees and organizers have a recognizable booking/pass use case, though the value proposition is relatively narrow and conventional.
impact_evidence: Ticket reservation and scannable personalized pass are explicit outcomes.
Standard/Premium/VIP ticket types indicate a concrete flow.
creativity_rationale: Agent-native event booking is a competent application of WebMCP, but the core reservation-and-QR pattern is familiar.
creativity_evidence: The agent-to-live-pass flow is a reasonable integration angle.
No unusual interaction model is evidenced.
usability_note: A short guided booking flow could be accessible, but validation and QR behavior are unobserved.
red_flags: No video frame sheets submitted; central booking and QR workflow is not demonstrated in the packet.
standouts: Clear concrete end state: a scannable event pass.
advance_reason: Plausible but conventional concept with thin execution evidence and only a moderate WebMCP delta.

one_line: ShopMate is a shared human-agent shopping workspace.
what_it_does: Offers catalog search, comparison, filtering, basket management, budgets, alternatives, and optimization through structured browser tools.
leverage_rationale: Shared shopping state and structured tools let agents search, compare, and manage a basket precisely while keeping the human in control; this is more than a chat overlay.
leverage_evidence: Eight structured tools are claimed for search, comparison, and shared shopping state.
Smart Basket supports quantities, budgets, alternatives, and optimization.
execution_rationale: Nine gallery images and a live demo support a fairly complete claimed surface, but no video or end-to-end transcript is present.
execution_evidence: Gallery covers homepage, catalog, WebMCP dashboard, activity, basket, and architecture.
Catalog is claimed to contain 58 products across seven categories.
impact_rationale: Shopping comparison and basket optimization address common consumer friction, especially when agents can handle repetitive research without taking control away from the person.
impact_evidence: Search/filter/sort/compare and basket workflows target recognizable shopping tasks.
Human-control framing is explicit.
creativity_rationale: The shared state and agent activity model add a meaningful angle to a familiar shopping assistant category.
creativity_evidence: Human, agent, and assistant planes are presented as a shared architecture.
Visible activity tracking connects agent actions to the UI.
usability_note: Catalog plus basket affordances are familiar and likely approachable; actual interaction quality is not directly observed.
red_flags: No submitted video; execution is inferred from gallery and description.
standouts: Broad, coherent shopping workflow rather than a single agent action.
advance_reason: Strong practical use case and well-scoped shared agent shopping experience.

one_line: Know Before Yes turns a software offer into a human-approved decision draft.
what_it_does: Agents inspect a bundled offer, find missing decisions, compare paths, stage a draft, and export only the exact revision a human approves.
leverage_rationale: The product's core trust boundary is implemented as shared structured state, typed rejection of premature actions, and human-only approval; generic UI driving would be materially less reliable and auditable.
leverage_evidence: Seven focused tools cover inspection, analysis, comparison, staging, approval status, commit, and export.
Premature commit/export return structured rejections without changing approved state.
Only visible human control can approve the exact staged revision.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a deliberate, internally consistent V1 workflow with strong state/authority semantics, but no visual frames were available to verify the full path.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repository are reported.
Default judge path is bounded to a bundled fictional vendor offer and explicit scenario constraints.
impact_rationale: Nontechnical small-business buyers face a real and costly problem in evaluating opaque software proposals; surfacing ownership, data, success, and support decisions is credible value.
impact_evidence: Problem statement names concrete unresolved decisions before purchase.
Exports a decision-ready Markdown or JSON draft without requiring an account or upload.
creativity_rationale: The agent-analyzes/human-approves interaction and exact-revision export is an original, safety-conscious application of WebMCP to procurement judgment.
creativity_evidence: Authority boundaries are part of the product interaction, not just documentation.
Source-bound missing decisions and staged revisions create a distinctive workflow.
usability_note: Bounded scenario flow and visible approval gate should support trust; actual UI clarity is unobserved.
red_flags: Bundled fictional offer limits real-world validation; no visual inspection was possible.
standouts: Excellent human authority and state-integrity design.
Concrete export semantics preserve exactly what was approved.
advance_reason: Distinctive high-leverage decision-support workflow with a real audience and unusually careful authority model.

one_line: HeatGrid is a shared emergency-operations planning board for heat response.
what_it_does: Combines human local inputs with agent-generated, constraint-aware cooling-center and shuttle allocations, stress tests, and audit trails.
leverage_rationale: The agent operates over shared operational context, constraints, deterministic allocation, and disruption testing while the human retains approval; structured state is central to the planning capability.
leverage_evidence: Six focused tools read context, inspect resources, apply constraints, draft plans, stress-test, and request review.
Plan metrics and audit trail appear immediately in the claimed shared dashboard.
No approval tool is exposed, preserving human authority.
execution_rationale: The scope is clearly bounded as a synthetic planning prototype and includes concrete plan metrics and failure testing, though the full visual workflow is not independently verifiable here.
execution_evidence: Live demo, public repository, and three video sheets are reported.
Demo claims HG-001 with coverage, equity, spend, trip, and zero-violation metrics, followed by bridge-closure stress test.
impact_rationale: Extreme-heat coordination is a serious, specific public-safety planning problem, and the proposed human-accountable planning support directly addresses combinatorial tradeoffs.
impact_evidence: Audience and constraints are concrete: coordinators balancing risk, capacity, routes, budget, accessibility, and bridge conditions.
Synthetic prototype is candidly distinguished from live dispatch or medical use.
creativity_rationale: The local-reality pinning plus accountable agent planning and stress testing is a strong, memorable interaction model for a high-stakes domain.
creativity_evidence: Human knowledge is explicitly entered as operational pins while agents handle combinatorics.
Stress-testing before human review is built into the narrative.
usability_note: Map/dashboard plus explicit review gate is a sensible coordinator workflow; accessibility and operational clarity remain unobserved.
red_flags: Synthetic data and planning-only scope mean real-world efficacy is unvalidated.
Visual evidence could not be independently assessed.
standouts: Concrete deterministic metrics and disruption stress test make the concept unusually accountable.
advance_reason: Exceptional audience/problem fit and transformative shared-state planning concept, with candid scope boundaries.

one_line: Agent-Readability Lab measures and improves whether agents can understand a live webpage.
what_it_does: Scores a page, tests it against real questions, rewrites the working copy, and rescores in the same browser session.
leverage_rationale: The product depends on an agent operating against the live editable page and immediately measuring the result; screenshots or generic UI automation cannot provide the same structured, same-session evaluation loop.
leverage_evidence: Tools are claimed for analyze, question testing, rewrite, and rescore against in-browser state.
The page being measured is the live working copy shared with the user.
execution_rationale: The workflow is conceptually coherent and the packet has a live demo and gallery images, but no video frames or transcript means end-to-end completion is only claimed.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repository are reported.
Description specifies before/after scoring and question-level failure proof.
impact_rationale: As agent-mediated discovery grows, site owners have a real need to know whether pages answer user questions and to repair failures.
impact_evidence: Targets website owners concerned with agent comprehension and visibility.
Produces actionable question-level failures rather than an opaque score.
creativity_rationale: Turning the agent's own live-page comprehension into a measurable, editable product loop is a notably original interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Analyze, test, rewrite, and rescore happen on the same page and session.
The tool evaluates actual questions instead of only static heuristics.
usability_note: Before/after score framing is understandable, but editing and question authoring details are unobserved.
red_flags: No submitted video frame sheets; claims about live rewriting and rescore are not independently demonstrated.
standouts: Strong recursive fit between product purpose and WebMCP mechanism.
Question-level proof is more useful than a generic readability grade.
advance_reason: Highly differentiated WebMCP-native dev tool with clear emerging need and a compelling interaction loop.

one_line: Quorum lets human and agent participants negotiate meeting times together.
what_it_does: Supports candidate slots, votes, reasons, counter-proposals, ranking, shared logs, and human organizer approval.
leverage_rationale: Multi-party negotiation with shared live state, agent participation, visible attribution, and human-only finalization is substantially more than an agent clicking a poll UI.
leverage_evidence: Seven tools cover state reading, joining, voting with reasons, counter-proposals, and ranking.
Every action lands in a shared HUMAN/AGENT negotiation log.
Only the human organizer can accept or lock the final time.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete stateful scheduler and supplies live demo, gallery, and frame-sheet references, though no transcript or observed visuals are available.
execution_evidence: Live demo and five gallery images are reported.
Claimed first-try four-tool chain demonstrates a concrete agent path.
impact_rationale: Scheduling across multiple people's constraints is common, tedious, and well matched to negotiation support; the audit log and approval boundary address trust.
impact_evidence: Human and agent participants can vote and counter-propose in one session.
Agent reasons and visible action log improve accountability.
creativity_rationale: Treating agents as equal negotiating participants rather than assistants that merely fill forms is a fresh and memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Mixed human/agent negotiation is the product's central concept.
Counter-proposals and reasons make the agent a participant in the social process.
usability_note: Normal poll-like UI plus agent automation should be approachable; real-time behavior is not independently observed.
red_flags: Frame-sheet and screenshot inspection was blocked by vision rate limiting.
standouts: Human approval remains explicit despite agent participation.
advance_reason: Strongly WebMCP-native collaboration concept with clear everyday value and a distinctive negotiation model.

one_line: Blnq Studio is an agent-accessible browser editor with live preview and built-in accessibility auditing.
what_it_does: Combines multi-file HTML/CSS/JS editing, live preview, WCAG audits, responsive preview, design-token checks, and WebMCP agent control.
leverage_rationale: A single shared editor/preview/audit state lets an agent build and immediately check accessibility and design-system compliance, closing tool handoffs that generic browser control handles poorly.
leverage_evidence: Editor, live preview, and WCAG audit are exposed to browser agents through WebMCP.
Every preview refresh runs claimed accessibility checks; design tokens and browser compatibility are integrated.
execution_rationale: The described scope is ambitious, but the submitted video's title is an unrelated Rick Astley video and there is no transcript, so execution evidence is materially undermined despite a coherent product description.
execution_evidence: Public demo facts report a 213-second video with unrelated title.
Description lists a broad integrated editor, preview, audit, viewport, and collaboration surface.
impact_rationale: Front-end developers and agent-assisted builders have a real need to catch accessibility regressions within the authoring loop rather than after handoff.
impact_evidence: Concrete target audience is front-end work involving multiple tabs and accessibility checks.
Violation panel is claimed to include impact, plain-English fix, and exact element.
creativity_rationale: Combining agent code authoring with immediate WCAG auditing and design-system enforcement in one shared browser surface is an ambitious, differentiated workflow.
creativity_evidence: Accessibility is positioned as part of the editing loop, not a separate checker.
DESIGN.md source-of-truth enforcement and baseline compatibility add depth.
usability_note: One-tab workflow could reduce handoffs, but the actual editor and audit behavior are not verified.
red_flags: Submitted video title is 'Rick Astley - Never Gonna Give You Up', unrelated to the claimed product.
No gallery images and no trustworthy video evidence; execution should not receive end-to-end credit.
standouts: Integrated design-system and compatibility checks are ambitious.
advance_reason: Interesting and potentially valuable concept, but the unrelated video submission creates a major eligibility/evidence problem and blocks confidence in execution.
